name: Cruzada
notes: Usual left-in-front Cruzada confirmed by the owner (2026-11-18): lead walks forward while follow walks back, then follow collects the left foot across in front of the right. Provisional clearance repair for subjective review: preserve the original closed entry, lead's 30 cm left-foot walk, two Q counts, body facings, flat rise and finishing support (both on left). Correct the follow's first step from forward to back, 40 cm, with 30 degrees of right-foot turnout. Her left foot then travels 23 cm to her right and 14 cm backward in her facing, on a shallow arc departing +100 degrees from her 180-degree body heading. It lands 3 cm across and 26 cm in front of the right, with 30 degrees of left-foot turnout. The turnout keeps the knees clear through the genuine cross; no pelvis offsets are needed. The deliberately crossed foot order is marked cross: true, but dense full-footprint and thigh/shin capsule tests cover the entire route without an interval exemption. Remove both partner-spacing and hold skipChecks. Default mannequins have over 1.4 cm full-leg clearance and 2.6 cm own-footprint clearance throughout linear/eased playback; hip lowering stays below 4 cm and lateral balance passes. The old follow exit was part of the direction bug and cannot be preserved: the corrected right foot ends at (0, 0.8), left at (-0.03, 0.54). Entry and lead landings remain unchanged. This intentionally ends crossed, not in a generic closed starting stance; existing Argentine tango sequence joins are already discontinuous and are outside this repair. Dimensions, turnout and route are modelling choices, not a syllabus transcription. No shared geometry, body or hold limits are changed.
